correctness.rationale: The exact geometric-sum Erlang MGF is (1-p)/((1-t/lambda)^s-p), yielding explicit mu1..mu4. The derivative of H3=B2 B4/B3^2 has numerator 2s(s-1)(s+1)Q_s with Q_s strictly positive for s>=3,x>=0, proving strict monotonicity and exact range. Its tail derivative integrates to the displayed cubic constant, and the inverse derivative follows by chain rule. Nonreal poles for p>0,s>=3 rule out finite acyclic PH representations. The standalone standard-library rational verifier passed 132 parameter cases and additional derivative checks; the universal algebraic factorization, not finite checking, is the proof.

The 2019 stochastic-order bounds are different inequalities and do not dominate the inverse map. We do not claim a general cyclic moment-ratio theorem.

value.rationale: The canonical fixed-length feedback cycle is genuinely non-acyclic and supplies a natural exactly solvable test family for higher-order PH moment inequalities and for PH moment-fitting consistency. Its exact H3 range and cubic flattening determine when H3-only inversion is feasible and numerically unreliable; this clarifies a concrete optimization objective near an exponential boundary. The lower-order H1 ratio already identifies p affinely, so cubic sensitivity is not claimed intrinsic to all full-moment estimators.
